extracted.intended_audience: taxonomists and authors publishing prokaryotic (bacterial/archaeal) names; IJSEM/IJSB authors; culture collection curators; members of ICSP/Judicial Commission
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and recommendations governing designation of types, valid/effective publication, priority, deposition of type strains, and citation for names of prokaryotic taxa (species up to higher ranks), used to determine whether a proposed name or nomenclatural action conforms to the Code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 15 — Designation of nomenclatural type
rubrics_metrics.description: For each named taxon of the various taxonomic categories there shall be designated a nomenclatural type. The nomenclatural type ... is that element of the taxon with which the name is permanently associated, whether as a correct name or as a later heterotypic synonym. The nomenclatural type is not necessarily the most typical or representative element of the taxon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Types are dealt with in Rules 16–22; types for categories are summarized in Table 2 (e.g. designated strain for species, type species for genus, genus for higher taxa).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 16 — Designation of type at time of publication in IJSEM
rubrics_metrics.description: After the date of publication of this Code, the type of a taxon must be designated by the author at the time the name of the taxon is published in the IJSEM (see Rules 15, 18a, b, f, 20a-c, 21a, 22, 27(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors who intend to publish name in IJSEM with reference to a previous effectively published description under Rule 27(2) are advised also to designate the type when publishing that description; if a previous effective publication does not designate a type then the type must be designated at valid publication in IJSEM.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 17 — Type determines application of name
rubrics_metrics.description: The type determines the application of the name of a taxon if the taxon is subsequently divided or united with another taxon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: when Bacillus was split, the genus containing the type species Bacillus subtilis must keep the name Bacillus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 18a — Type of a species/subspecies should be a designated strain
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever possible, the type of a species or subspecies is a designated strain. The type strain is made up of living cultures descended from the strain designated as the nomenclatural type. The strain should have been maintained in pure culture and should agree closely to its characters with those in the original description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Type strain may be designated in various ways (see 18b–18d). (1) Until 31 Dec 2000 a description/preserved specimen/illustration could serve as type if no culture existed. (2) As from 1 Jan 2001 description/preserved specimen/illustration may not serve as the type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 18b — Holotype by original designation
rubrics_metrics.description: If the author in the effective publication of the name of a species or subspecies definitely designated a type strain, then this strain shall be accepted as the type strain and may be referred to as the holotype.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original author's explicit designation of a strain establishes the holotype.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 18c — Designation and establishment of a neotype
rubrics_metrics.description: If a strain on which the original description was based cannot be found, a neotype strain may be proposed. A neotype strain must be proposed in the IJSEM, together with citation of the author(s) of the name, a description or reference to an effectively published description, and a record of the permanently established culture collection(s) where the strain is deposited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author should show that a careful search for original strains has been made and none found and that proposed neotype agrees closely with original description. A proposed neotype becomes established two years after publication in the IJSEM provided no objections (which must be referred within first year to the Judicial Commission). Note defines 'strain' broadly as culture or subcultures derived from original strain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 18d — Suggested neotype has no standing until formal proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: A strain suggested as a neotype but not formally proposed in accordance with Rule 18c (suggested neotype) has no standing in nomenclature until formally proposed and established.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Informal suggestions do not affect nomenclature; formal IJSEM proposal required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 18e — Discovery of original strain after neotype proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: If an original strain that should constitute the type of a species is discovered subsequent to the formal proposal or establishment of a neotype for that species, the matter shall be referred immediately to the Judicial Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judicial Commission decides appropriate action when originals reappear after neotype actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 18f — Replacement of description/specimen by type strain once cultivated
rubrics_metrics.description: If a description or illustration constitutes, or a dead preserved specimen has been designated the type of a species (Rule 18a(1)) and later a strain of this species is cultivated, then the type strain may be designated by the person who isolated the strain or by a subsequent author. This type strain shall then replace the description, illustration or preserved specimen as the nomenclatural type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designation must be published in IJSEM; authorship and date of priority determined by effective and valid publication of original name (Rule 24b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 18g — Unsuitable type or neotype strains
rubrics_metrics.description: If a type or neotype strain has become unsuitable owing to changes in its characters or for other reasons, then the matter should be referred to the Judicial Commission, which may decide to take action leading to replacement of the strain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judicial Commission handles replacement when strains change or become unsuitable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 19 — Reference strains
rubrics_metrics.description: A reference strain is a strain that is neither a type nor a neotype strain but a strain used in comparative studies, e.g. taxonomic or serological, or for chemical assay. A reference strain has no standing in nomenclature, but it may, by subsequent action, be made a neotype.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference strains are useful comparators but do not confer nomenclatural status unless later formalized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 20a — Type species for a genus/subgenus
rubrics_metrics.description: The nomenclatural type of a genus or subgenus is the type species, that is, the single species or one of the species included when the name was originally validly published. Only species whose names are legitimate may serve as types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Type species is chosen from species included at original publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 20b — Original author's designation of type species
rubrics_metrics.description: If the author of the effective or valid publication of a generic or subgeneric name designated a type species, that species shall be accepted as the type species.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original explicit designation by author fixes type species.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 20c — Genus with only one species
rubrics_metrics.description: If the genus when originally published included only one species, then that species is the type species.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monotypic genus automatically has its sole species as type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 20d — Designation by subsequent author
rubrics_metrics.description: The type species shall be selected from one of the species included when the genus was originally published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation 20d: authors are recommended to exclude doubtful, inadequately characterized, doubtfully referred, definitely disagreeing, or exceptional species from consideration when selecting the type; examples given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 20e — International agreement for fixing type species or rejecting generic names
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) If none of the species named by an author can be recognized and no identifiable type species can be selected, the Judicial Commission may issue an Opinion declaring the generic name rejected (nomen rejiciendum). (2) If later-named identifiable species exist, one of these may be selected as the type species and established by Opinion of the Judicial Commission; the generic name is then ascribed to the author of the species selected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples cited (Gaffkya rejection; Vibrio example).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 20f — Retention of type species when substituting generic name
rubrics_metrics.description: The valid publication of a new generic name as a deliberate substitute for an earlier one does not change the type species of the genus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Xanthomonas created as substitute for Phytomonas retains the same type species.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 20g — Genus and its type subgenus share same type species
rubrics_metrics.description: A genus and its type subgenus share the same type species.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example given (Moraxella lacunata).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 21a — Type of taxon from genus to order is type genus
rubrics_metrics.description: The nomenclatural type of a taxon above genus, up to and including order, is the legitimate name of the included genus on whose name the name of the relevant taxon is based. One taxon of each category must include the type genus. The names of the taxa which include the type genus must be formed by the addition of the appropriate suffix to the stem of the name of the type genus (see Rule 9).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Pseudomonas is type genus for Pseudomonadales (order), etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 21b — Fixing type genus by Opinion when family name conserved
rubrics_metrics.description: If the name of a family was not made in conformity with Rule 21a but its name has been conserved, then the type genus may be fixed by an Opinion of the Judicial Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Escherichia is the type genus of Enterobacteriaceae (Opinion cited).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 22 — Type of taxa higher than order
rubrics_metrics.description: The type of a taxon higher than order is one of the contained orders, and if there is only one order this becomes the type. If there are two or more orders the type shall be designated by the author at the time of the proposal of the name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not designated, type may be later designated by an Opinion of the Judicial Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 23a — Priority: single correct name rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Each taxon above species, up to and including order, with a given circumscription, position, and rank can bear only one correct name, that is, the earliest that is in accordance with the Rules of this Code. The name of a species is a binary combination of a generic name and specific epithet. In a given position, a species can bear only one correct epithet, that is, the earliest that is in accordance with the Rules of this Code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes: apply Rule 23a independently to generic name and specific epithet for species transfers; subspecies names are ternary combinations; priority dates discussed (1 Jan 1980 change) and Judicial Commission can make exceptions by conserving or rejecting names (nomina conservanda/rejicienda). Definitions of legitimate/illegitimate/effectively_published/validly_published/correct included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 23b — Date of name is date of valid publication; only legitimate names count for priority
rubrics_metrics.description: The date of a name or epithet is that of its valid publication. For purposes of priority, however, only legitimate names and epithets are taken into consideration (see Rules 32b and 54).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Valid publication date matters for priority; illegitimate names are excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 24a — Priority and Approved Lists (1 Jan 1980 baseline)
rubrics_metrics.description: Valid publication of names (or epithets) which are in accordance with the Rules of this Code dates from the date of publication of the Code. Priority of publication dates from 1 January 1980. On that date all names published prior to 1 January 1980 and included in the Approved Lists of Bacterial Names are treated ... as though they had been validly published for the first time on that date, the existing types being retained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Names prior to 1 Jan 1980 not on Approved Lists have no further standing; Approved Lists contain references to descriptions and types; neotypes may be proposed on such lists; homotypic synonyms may appear on Approved Lists; reuse of pre-1980 names not on Approved Lists is allowed but discouraged if confusing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 24b — Determination of priority between competing names
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) If two names compete for priority and both date from 1 Jan 1980 on an Approved List, priority shall be determined by date of effective publication before 1 Jan 1980; if same date by page number then order of publication. (2) If two names published after 1 Jan 1980 compete, priority is determined by date of valid publication or announcement in IJSEM; same issue/page numbers resolved by page number or order in original articles; Validation Lists sequence number used where relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Validation List sequence numbers reflect date of receipt of validation request; multiple examples illustrating priority resolution provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 24c — Rejection of names previously on Approved Lists
rubrics_metrics.description: The Judicial Commission may place on the list of rejected names (nomina rejicienda) a name previously published in an Approved List.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judicial Commission has authority to reject previously accepted names by Opinion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 25a — Effective publication requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective publication is effected under this Code by making generally available, by sale or distribution, to the scientific community, printed and/or electronic material for the purpose of providing a permanent record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a name is published in a language unfamiliar to the majority of workers in bacteriology, it is recommended to include a description in English. Note: electronic publication should follow traditions acceptable to the Code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 25b — Non-accepted forms of publication
rubrics_metrics.description: No other kind of publication than that cited in Rule 25a is accepted as effective, nor are the following: (1) communication of new names at meetings, meeting minutes, or (after 1950) abstracts presented at meetings; (2) placing names on specimens or listings/catalogues; (3) microfilm/microcard reproductions; (4) ephemeral publications, newsletters, newspapers after 1900, or non-scientific periodicals; (5) inclusion of a name of a new taxon of prokaryote in a published patent application or issued patent; (6) making available electronic material in advance of publication (papers in press, unpublished manuscripts in electronic format).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly excludes patents and other ephemeral or non-distributed means as effective publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 26a — Date of publication
rubrics_metrics.description: The date of publication of a scientific work is the date of publication of the printed and/or electronic matter. The date given to the work containing the name or epithet must be regarded as correct in the absence of proof to the contrary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes publication date principle for priority purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 26b — Acceptance date irrelevant to effective date
rubrics_metrics.description: The date of acceptance of an article for publication if given in a publication does not indicate the effective date of publication and has no significance in the determination of the priority of publication of names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only the actual publication date counts, not acceptance date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 27 — Conditions for valid publication of a new name or new combination
rubrics_metrics.description: A name of a new taxon, or a new combination for an existing taxon, is not validly published unless the following criteria are met: (1) The name is published in the IJSB/IJSEM. (2) The publication is accompanied by a description of the taxon or by a reference to a previous effectively published description of the taxon. As of 1 Jan 2001 the following criteria also apply: (a) The new name or new combination should be clearly stated and indicated as such (e.g., sp. nov., comb. nov.). (b) The derivation (etymology) of a new name (and if necessary of a new combination) must be given. (c) The properties of the taxon being described must be given directly after (a) and (b). (d) All information in (c) should be accessible. (3) The type of the taxon must be designated. In case of species/subspecies including new combinations, type strains must be deposited according to Rule 30.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note 1: valid publication requires publication in IJSB/IJSEM and reference to an effectively published description; date of valid publication is date in IJSB/IJSEM. Responsibility primarily lies with the author but others may submit names for valid publication if they conform. Notification Lists exist but have no formal status except for orthographic corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 28a — Revival of pre-1980 names (nom. rev.)
rubrics_metrics.description: An author validly publishing a new name after 1 Jan 1980 may revive a name published prior to 1 Jan 1980 but not listed in the Approved Lists unless the name is a nomen rejiciendum. Authority for the name must be claimed by the new author. If reviving with same circumscription/position/rank, may append 'nom. rev.' The proposal must contain a brief diagnosis stating features that justify revival; description and derivation must conform to Rule 27(2); type must be designated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revived names are treated as new names and require valid publication; date of priority is publication in IJSEM. Search for pre-1980 publications is no longer required; Approved Lists form foundation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 28b — Circumstances rendering a name not validly published
rubrics_metrics.description: A name or epithet is not validly published in the following circumstances: (1) It was not accepted at the time of publication by the author who published it (e.g., published with question mark or indication of doubt). (2) It was merely proposed in anticipation of future acceptance or future discovery. (3) It was mentioned incidentally—an author did not clearly state or indicate that he is proposing a new name or combination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided for each circumstance (Muellerina, Clostridium example, incidental mentions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 29 — Valid publication of a genus or subgenus
rubrics_metrics.description: For a generic or subgeneric name to be validly published it must comply with: (1) publication in conformity with Rules 27 and 28b; (2) the genus/subgenus named must include one or more described or previously described species. Instead of a new description, citation to a previously and effectively published description may be given. In case of a genus with a single species, a combined generic and specific description may be given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation 29: a description should mention points in which the genus differs from related genera and, where possible, the family should be mentioned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 30 — Conditions for valid publication of a species name and deposition requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: For the name of a species to be validly published, it must: (1) be published in conformity with Rules 27 and 28b; (2) be published as a binary combination (genus + specific epithet); (3)(a) Up to 31 Dec 2000, before publication, a culture of the type strain (or if non-cultivable, type material/photo/illustration) should be deposited in at least one permanently established culture collection and the collection designation quoted. (b) As of 1 Jan 2001, the description of a new species (or new combinations previously represented by viable cultures) must include the designation of a type strain, and a viable culture of that strain must be deposited in at least two publicly accessible culture collections in different countries; designations should be quoted and evidence presented that cultures are present, viable, and available at time of publication. (4) Organisms deposited with access restrictions (e.g., safe deposits or strains deposited solely for current patent purposes) may not serve as type strains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions for specialized facilities (e.g., BSL-3, high pressure) may be considered individually by committee; Recommendation 30: descriptions should conform at least to minimal standards for the relevant taxon; Note 1: minimal standards lists are being prepared; Note 2: minimal standards guide but should not contradict Principle 1(4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 31a — Ambiguous descriptions invalidate publication
rubrics_metrics.description: The name of a species or a subspecies is not validly published if the description is demonstrably ambiguous and cannot be critically identified for purposes of the precise application of the name of a taxon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples illustrate ambiguous consortium descriptions vs legitimate species descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 31b — Consortium names not regulated
rubrics_metrics.description: The name of a consortium is not regulated by this Code, and such a name has no standing in nomenclature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A consortium is an aggregate or association of two or more organisms (example provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 32a — Valid publication of a subspecies name
rubrics_metrics.description: For the name of a subspecies to be validly published, it must: (1) be published in conformity with Rules 27 and 28b; (2) be published as a ternary combination (generic name + specific epithet + subspecific epithet) with 'subsp.' between specific and subspecific epithets; (3) the author must clearly indicate that a subspecies is being named.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation 32a: Recommendations 30a and 30b apply to subspecies with 'species' replaced by 'subspecies'. Example format given (Bacillus subtilis subsp. subtilis).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 32b — Epithet publication with illegitimate generic name
rubrics_metrics.description: A specific (or subspecific) epithet is not rendered illegitimate by publication in a species (or subspecies) name in which the generic name is illegitimate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that epithet legitimacy is independent of illegitimacy of the generic name in which it was published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 33a — Indication of proposing a new name
rubrics_metrics.description: An author should indicate that a name is being proposed for a new taxon by the addition of the appropriate abbreviation for the category to which the taxon belongs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appropriate abbreviations listed (ord. nov., gen. nov., sp. nov., comb. nov.); notes on typographic convention (Latin abbreviations often printed in Roman or boldface to differentiate from the Latin name). Examples provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 33b — Citation of author(s) and year for a taxon name
rubrics_metrics.description: The citation of the name of a taxon that has been previously proposed should include both the name of the author(s) who first published the name and the year of publication. If there are more than two authors, citation includes only the first author followed by 'et al.' and the year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correct citation enables verification of publication date and original description and helps distinguish usage by different authors; examples provided.
